cards.text: The LORD has already told Moses about the offerings. Now He gives Moses the law for each one, to command Aaron and his sons, the priests. First up is the burnt offering, and it stays on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning.

cards.question: The burnt offering stays on the altar all night. What does God say about the altar fire?

answers.text: It must be put out at night
It must be lit fresh each morning

cards.text: Morning comes, and it's cleanup time. The priest puts on his linen robe and linen undergarments, removes the ashes from the altar, and places them beside it.

cards.question: True or false: The priest keeps his linen robe on when he carries the ashes away.
The priest changes into other clothes and picks up the ashes from beside the altar. Where does he carry them?

answers.text: To a clean place outside the camp
To the banks of the Jordan

cards.text: Back at the altar, the fire has to keep burning. So every morning, the priest gets it ready for the offerings.

cards.question: To keep the altar fire going, every morning the priest is to add ___ to the fire.

cards.text: He arranges the burnt offering on it and burns the fat portions of the peace offerings, and God says it twice: the fire must not be extinguished. Me? I set THREE timers and I still forget my oven.
Next comes the law of the grain offering. The priest burns a handful of the fine flour and oil, with all the frankincense, as the memorial portion, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

cards.question: Once that handful of the grain offering is burned, what happens to the rest of it?

answers.text: Aaron and his sons eat it
It is burned the next morning
It goes back to the giver

cards.question: True or false: The priests may bake their share of the grain offering with leaven.

cards.text: They eat it in a holy place, the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, and God calls it most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering. It's a permanent portion for Aaron's sons for the generations to come, and friend, I can't keep a cookie on my counter for ten minutes.

Then the LORD tells Moses about the grain offering Aaron and his sons present on the day he is anointed, half in the morning and half in the evening. Fine flour, oil, a griddle, well-kneaded, broken in pieces: friend, NOW you're speaking my language.

cards.question: The priests get to eat most grain offerings. But what happens to every grain offering for a priest?

answers.text: It is eaten by the high priest
It is shared with the people

cards.text: Next comes the law of the sin offering, and it is most holy. It's slaughtered before the LORD in the same place the burnt offering is slaughtered.

cards.question: Once the sin offering is offered, who eats it?

cards.text: Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and the clay pot it's boiled in must be broken. BROKEN! They shoved me in a junk drawer, but nobody ever smashed me.

cards.question: A clay pot used for the sin offering gets broken. What about a bronze pot?

answers.text: It is scoured and rinsed with water
It is broken just the same
It is melted down for the altar

cards.question: True or false: A sin offering may still be eaten even if its blood was brought into the Holy Place to make atonement.

cards.text: The LORD is still giving Moses the law of each offering for the priests. Now it's the guilt offering, which is most holy. It's slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered, its blood is splattered on all sides of the altar, and all its fat is burned as a food offering to the LORD.

cards.question: God says the guilt offering is like the ___ offering, and the same law applies to both.

cards.text: Then God spells out what the priests keep, starting with the hide of a burnt offering for the priest who presents it. Any grain offering baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it too.

cards.question: True or false: Grain offerings that are dry or mixed with oil also go only to the priest who presents them.

cards.text: If someone offers a peace offering in thanksgiving, he brings unleavened cakes, unleavened wafers, cakes of fine flour and cakes of leavened bread along with it. Cakes, wafers, MORE cakes: friend, I have never felt so at home in Leviticus.

cards.question: From the thanksgiving cakes, one portion of each offering is a contribution to the LORD. Who does it belong to?

answers.text: The priest who sprinkles the blood
The man who brought the offering

cards.question: And the meat of that peace offering of thanksgiving? When must it be eaten?

answers.text: On the day it is offered
Within three days of the offering

cards.question: True or false: Meat from a peace offering given as a vow or a freewill offering may also be eaten the next day.
Some meat from a peace offering is still left on the third day. What must happen to it?

answers.text: It is given to the poor

cards.text: Eat it on the third day and it will not be accepted; it shall be an abomination, and the one who eats it shall bear his iniquity. Day-three cookies I'll still eat, but this meat? Hands OFF.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten, so it gets burned up. Any other meat, anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat.

cards.question: What happens to someone who is unclean and eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD?

answers.text: That person is cut off from his people
That person must pay back a fifth more
That person must wash and wait till evening

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses a word for all the Israelites: they are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep or a goat. Fat from an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts can be used for other things, but they must not eat it.

cards.question: Along with the fat, God says Israel must not eat the ___ of any bird or animal in any of their dwellings.

cards.text: Back to the peace offering, and who gets what. The one bringing it carries the fat and the breast with his own hands, and waves the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.

cards.question: The priest burns the fat of the peace offering on the altar. Who gets the breast that was waved?
True or false: The right thigh of the peace offering goes to the priest who presents its blood and fat.

cards.text: God says He has given the breast and the thigh to Aaron and his sons as a permanent portion from the sons of Israel, ever since the day they were anointed. And that's the law of the burnt, grain, sin, guilt, ordination and peace offerings, friend, and I didn't drop a single crumb.

cards.question: Where did the LORD give Moses all these laws of the offerings?

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time in the walkthrough, but the card doesn't say who he is. Aaron is introduced as one of the priests, but Moses is not.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Morning comes, and it's cleanup time" puts the removal of the ashes in the morning. Leviticus 6:10 gives no time for removing the ashes. Verse 9 says only that the offering stays on the altar until morning.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The core action is keeping a fire burning so it never goes out. "I set THREE timers and I still forget my oven" is about forgetting an oven, which suggests leaving something burning or forgetting cookies inside. That is close to the opposite action, so the comparison doesn't click without explaining.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card carries three things: the portion is eaten in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, it is most holy like the sin and guilt offerings, and it is a permanent portion for the generations to come. A joke is added on top of these.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "They shoved me in a junk drawer" casts the Millers as rough with him. His backstory says he was slid into the drawer. The line reads as a grudge instead of kindness.

rule.text: Godly character. He never holds a grudge, and his humor reflects kindness and forgiveness.

findings.problem: The story card runs three sentences and carries more than two things happening. The guilt offering is most holy, it is slaughtered where the burnt offering is, its blood is splattered on all sides of the altar, and all its fat is burned.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card cites Leviticus 7:22-25 but tells only 7:22-24. It never mentions 7:25, where anyone who eats the fat is cut off from his people. The citation should be Leviticus 7:22-24.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The whole passage is rules for offerings. The long-stretch rule lists "rules for offerings and feasts" as a long stretch that gets one summary card and never a choice card. The walkthrough instead gives these rules many story cards and choice cards. If the rule were applied literally, the passage would shrink to almost nothing.
findings.question: When an entire passage is one of the listed long-stretch kinds, like rules for offerings, should it be walked through as key laws with choice cards, or summed up under the long-stretch rule? If it is walked through, how much detail should get choice cards?
